'''Ellen Druffel''' is an American [[oceanography|oceanographer]] and [[isotope geochemistry|isotope geochemist]] known for her research using radiocarbon to track marine processes. Druffel was born in Los Angeles, CA, but raised in Pasadena.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ellen R. M. Druffel – NAS |url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/ellen-r-m-druffel-ixeawr/ |access-date=2026-04-10 |website=www.nasonline.org |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Career==

Druffel is a professor who holds the Fred Kavli Endowed Chair in Earth System Science at [[U.C. Irvine]], where she was one of the department's founding faculty members.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ellen R.M. Druffel – UC Irvine School of Physical Sciences |url=https://ps.uci.edu/fprofile/ellen-r-m-druffel/ |access-date=2026-04-10 |language=en-US}}</ref> She received a B.S. in chemistry from [[Loyola Marymount University]] in 1975 and a PhD in chemistry in 1980 from the Department of Chemistry at [[U.C. San Diego]],<ref>{{cite web |title=Ellen R.M. Druffel |url=https://sites.uci.edu/druffel/ |accessdate=25 June 2025 |website=Druffel Research Group}}</ref> where her Ph.D. advisor was [[Hans Suess]].

==Awards==

In 1990, Druffel received the [[James B. Macelwane Medal]] from the [[American Geophysical Union]]. Druffel is a fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] (2001), and a fellow of The Oceanography Society (2009).<ref>{{Cite web|title=tos-fellows-meet {{!}} The Oceanography Society|url=https://tos.org/tos-fellows-meet|access-date=2021-04-27|website=tos.org|archive-date=2021-06-15|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210615072322/https://tos.org/tos-fellows-meet|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2004 she was awarded the Ruth Patrick Award from the [[American Society of Limnology and Oceanography]].  The Ruth Patrick Award is given "to honor outstanding research by a scientist in the application of basic aquatic science principles to the identification, analysis and/or solution of important environmental problems.".<ref name=aslo>{{cite web |url=http://aslo.org/awards/patrick.html |title=Ruth Patrick award |website=ASLO |accessdate=11 May 2017 |archive-date=18 May 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170518105759/http://www.aslo.org/awards/patrick.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> Druffel's Ruth Patrick award acknowledged "her sustained critical contributions on the composition and age of dissolved, particulate, and sedimentary carbon and for furthering the understanding of the processes governing the fate and distribution of oceanic carbon and the important role that the oceans play in global carbon flux."<ref name=aslo /> In 2016 she was awarded the [[Roger Revelle Medal]] from the American Geophysical Union.<ref name=eos>{{cite web |url=https://eos.org/agu-news/2016-agu-union-medal-award-and-prize-recipients-announced |title=2016 AGU Union Medal, Award, and Prize Recipients Announced |first1=Margaret |last1=Leinen |first2=Sam |last2=Mukasa |date=21 July 2016 |website=EOS |publisher=American Geophysical Union |accessdate=11 May 2017}}</ref> Druffel was elected to the National Academy of Sciences in 2020.<ref>{{Cite web|title=2020 NAS Election|url=http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/2020-nas-election.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200428010617/http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/2020-nas-election.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=April 28, 2020|access-date=2021-04-26|website=www.nasonline.org}}</ref>

==Research==
Druffel's research uses radiocarbon to track marine processes, focusing in two areas: coral paleoclimate records and marine organic matter carbon cycling. She is the author of more than 180 publications in the scientific literature.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=cTL5dS4AAAAJ&hl=en/ |title=Ellen R. M. Druffel |website=Google Scholar |accessdate=11 May 2017 }}</ref>
